Soils are one of SoNaRR's three cross-cutting natural resources but are foregrounded by no strategic indicator, which is why the scan missed this until the soil_land cluster was added on 24 July 2026. Supports SI2 and SI4 if the recommendations are taken up, since soil condition drives both habitat restoration and diffuse pollution. The live hook is now delivery: whether soil-loss protections are actually added to the Control of Agricultural Pollution Regulations, and the SLM soil health indicator the response said would be laid with Agriculture Act indicators and targets. With the missing-response hook gone, this reads as a watch item rather than a follow-up.
summary: The Senedd's Economy, Trade and Rural Affairs Committee published 'Digging the dirt: Improving Wales' soil health' on 18 November 2025, after evidence sessions in May and June 2025, with 7 recommendations and 6 conclusions. The Welsh Government responded on 16 January 2026 and the report was debated in Plenary on 4 February 2026. It accepted the call to set out its regulatory plans, including putting the GAEC 4 and 5 soil standards on a statutory footing, pointing to the Control of Agricultural Pollution Regulations review recommendation to add soil-loss protections to those regulations; accepted in principle sharing SFS soil test data, but only aggregated through the ERAMMP national monitoring programme; accepted in principle the call for a voluntary minimum soil health standard while saying its new Sustainable Land Management soil health indicator will not create one; and rejected a planning framework to protect the best agricultural land. The Agricultural Soil Policy Statement (28 April 2025) is the current policy baseline.
title: Senedd committee report 'Digging the dirt' calls for statutory soil health standards; Welsh Government response of 16 January 2026 accepts most but declines a minimum soil standard
